checks.do: Which items the navigation page lists under Administration (other pages place further items there), and which browsers the portal supports.
How long resolved and IaC notifications are kept.
Whether the event falls in the 60 days of audit logs the portal shows.

first-login.statement: After an organization is provisioned for ZPC, the administrator receives an email with the tenant ID and a link to reset the password, and signs in with the registered email ID as Login ID.

quotes: After your organization is provisioned for Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC), you will receive an email with the tenant ID and a link to reset the password
Enter your Login ID. This is your registered email ID.

eusa.statement: The ZPC Admin Portal displays the End User Subscription Agreement (EUSA) at first login; clicking Cancel logs the user out automatically.

quotes: When you log in for the first time, the ZPC Admin Portal displays the EUSA.
If you click Cancel, the ZPC Admin Portal logs you out automatically.

admin-menu.statement: The Administration item of the ZPC Admin Portal is where Cloud Accounts, Version Control & CI/CD Systems, Workstations & IDEs, Container Registry & Workloads, Integrations, Business Unit Management, Audit Logs, Single Sign On, Scheduled Reports and API Keys are configured and managed.

quotes: Click Administration to configure and manage Cloud Accounts, Version Control & CI/CD Systems, Workstations & IDEs, Container Registry & Workloads, Integrations, Business Unit Management, Audit Logs, Single Sign On, Scheduled Reports, and API Keys.

browsers.statement: ZPC supports Chrome, Firefox and Edge (two most recent versions of each) on Windows 10 and 11, and Chrome, Firefox and Safari (two most recent versions of each) on OS X and macOS; older versions and other browsers should be compatible but are not actively tested.

quotes: Google Chrome (two most recent versions)
Mozilla Firefox (two most recent versions)
Microsoft Edge (two most recent versions)

mac-os-versions.statement: ZPC lists OS X 9, OS X 10 and macOS 10 as the supported Apple operating systems.

quotes: ZPC supports the following Apple operating systems:
- OS X 9
- OS X 10
- macOS 10

profile.statement: The My Profiles page shows the email address, group, role, My Tenants and My Downloads; a user in several groups sees the list of groups and selects one to access ZPC modules by that group's roles and permissions.

quotes: Email Address: Your registered email address.
Group: The group to which your account belongs.
Role: The role associated with the group.
My Tenants: The tenants that are assigned to your account.
My Downloads: View the list of reports you've requested to download.
If you are assigned to multiple user groups, then the list of groups is displayed. You can select the required group to access ZPC modules based on the group's roles and permissions.

tables.statement: Table settings changed in the ZPC Admin Portal are stored in the browser's local storage and are lost if the cache is cleared or another browser is used; Reset on the column menu does not reset the sort order.

quotes: Every time you make a change, the settings are stored in your browser's local storage so that your changes are preserved the next time you log on.
If you clear your cache or use a different browser, your settings are lost.
Click the Column Menu icon, then click Reset.
This will not reset your sort order.

common-filters.statement: ZPC offers four filters by default: Business Units, Cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes), Accounts (selectable by account name or ID) and Regions.

quotes: The following filters are available by default:
Business Units: Returns results only from selected business units.
Cloud: Returns results only from selected cloud service providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes).
Accounts: Returns results only from selected cloud accounts. You can select cloud accounts using either the cloud account name or the cloud account ID.
Regions: Returns results only from selected regions.

help-browser.statement: The Help Browser is available on all pages of the ZPC Admin Portal; customizations are kept until logout or session expiry, and closing it clears the navigation history.

quotes: The Zscaler Help Browser is available for all pages within the Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) Admin Portal.
Zscaler saves your customization until you log out or the session expires.
Closing the Help Browser clears your navigation history.

guide-subscription.statement: According to the step-by-step guide, the IaC feature and the Vulnerability Integration feature are available based on the ZPC subscription.

quotes: The Infrastructure as Code (IaC) feature is available based on your ZPC subscription.
The Vulnerability Integration feature is available based on your ZPC subscription.

guide-policies.statement: The step-by-step guide says ZPC offers over 400 security policies across multiple cloud service providers, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform.

quotes: ZPC offers over 400 security policies across multiple cloud service providers (CSPs), including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.

guide-steps.statement: The step-by-step guide lists Step 1 log in to the ZPC Admin Portal, Step 2 onboard cloud accounts, Step 3 configure administrators and roles, Step 4 configure single sign-on, and Steps 6 to 11 for alert rules, security policies, third-party integrations, scheduled reports, IaC integrations and vulnerability integrations.

quotes: Step 1: Log in to ZPC Admin Portal
Step 2: Onboard Cloud Accounts
Step 3: Configure Administrators & Roles
Step 4: Configure Single-Sign-On Authentication
Step 6: Configure Alerts Rules
Step 7: Manage Security Policies
Step 8: Configure 3rd-Party Integrations
Step 9: Configure Scheduled Reports
Step 10: Configure IaC Integrations
Step 11: Configure Vulnerability Integrations

guide-third-party.statement: ZPC sends data logs (alerts) to cloud storage services such as Amazon S3 buckets, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk or Amazon Security Lake, and offers incident management by integrating with ITSM tools, cloud storage services and ChatOps tools.

quotes: ZPC integrates with your cloud storage services, such as Amazon S3 buckets, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk, or Amazon Security Lake, and sends data logs (alerts) to these storage services.
ZPC offers incident management by integrating with ITSM tools, cloud storage services, and ChatOps tools.

notification-triggers.statement: The Notification Center reports whether ZPC lost connectivity with the public cloud infrastructure, reports were not delivered, alerts were not sent to third-party tools, and vulnerability or IaC scans failed with the reason.

quotes: Check if the ZPC service has lost connectivity with the public cloud infrastructure.
Check if the reports are not delivered.
Check if the alerts are not sent to third-party tools.
Check if the vulnerability scans fail and the reason for failure.
Check if the IaC scans fail and the reason for failure.

notification-retention.statement: ZPC automatically deletes resolved notifications after 30 days and deletes a cloud account's notifications when the account is deleted; IaC notifications are retained only for 7 days.

quotes: ZPC automatically deletes resolved notifications after 30 days.
If you delete any cloud account, then ZPC automatically deletes the notifications.
IaC notifications are retained only for 7 days and then the logs are not displayed in the ZPC Admin Portal.

notification-fields.statement: Each notification shows Module (Data Collection or Vulnerability Management), Severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low) and Status (Open, Resolved).

quotes: Module: The module (Data Collection or Vulnerability Management) for which the notification is detected.
Severity: The severity of the notification (Critical, High, Medium, and Low).
Status: The status of the notification (Open, Resolved).

audit-retention.statement: Administrators can view the audit logs for the past 60 days.

quotes: Administrators can view the audit logs for the past 60 days.

audit-fields.statement: Each audit log event shows Event ID, Event Timestamp in UTC, Tenant Name, User, Login Type (Local or SAML), Interface, Role Name, IP, User Agent, Action, Data Object Type, Data Object Name, Module and Sub Module.

quotes: Event ID: The unique identifier for the event.
User: The email ID of the administrator who initiated the action.
IP: The IP address of the interface where the administrator performs the action.
Action: The action performed by the administrator.
Module: The module (e.g., Administration, Alerts, Investigation, etc.) that was accessed in the ZPC Admin Portal.
Event Timestamp: The date and time in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), when the event occurred.
Tenant Name: The name of the ZPC tenant.
Login Type: The type of login (Local or SAML) that was initiated.
Interface: The type of interface (browser, virtual machine, etc.) that is used to sign in to the ZPC Admin Portal.
Role Name: The role assigned to the user.
User Agent: The browser application that was used to perform the action.
Data Object Type: The object (e.g., Alert Rule, Custom Policy, IaC Integration, etc.) within the module on which the action is being performed.
Data Object Name: The name (e.g., the policy name that was disabled) of the object specified by the user.
Sub Module: The sub-module (e.g., security policies, cloud alerts, etc.) that was accessed within the module in the ZPC Admin Portal.

audit-export-filter.statement: Audit log data can be exported to a CSV file and filtered, for example with the Event Time filter to see the last 24 hours.

quotes: Export the audit log data to a CSV file.
For example, you can set the Event Time filter to view the logs that were recorded in the last 24 hours.

audit-what-is-logged.statement: Audit logs record sign-in and sign-out attempts, adding or removing cloud accounts, configuring alerts, IaC integrations, vulnerability management, enabling or disabling policies, downloading reports and configuration changes during a session.

quotes: The logs are captured for several actions, including sign-in and sign-out attempts, adding or removing cloud accounts, configuring alerts, IaC integrations, vulnerability management, enabling or disabling policies, downloading reports, etc., including any configuration changes that users handled during a session.

audit-event-modules.statement: ZPC records actions in the Administration, Alerts, IaC Integration, Policies, Reports, Vulnerability Management and Kubernetes Cluster modules.

quotes: ZPC records various actions performed by administrators in the following modules and displays the list in a chronological order on the Audit Logs page:
- Administration
- Alerts
- IaC Integration
- Policies
- Reports
- Vulnerability Management
- Kubernetes Cluster

audit-sso-events.statement: The audit log events include Edit SSO, Enable SSO for Group, Disable SSO, Delete SSO and Enable Just-in-Time (JIT) Provisioning.

quotes: - Edit SSO
- Enable SSO for Group
- Disable SSO
- Delete SSO
- Enable Just-in-Time (JIT) Provisioning

audit-iac-policy-events.statement: The audit log events under IaC Policies include Allow Policy and Skip Policy.

quotes: - IaC Policies
- Allow Policy
- Skip Policy

audit-api-key-name.statement: The name given to an API key appears in the audit logs as the entity performing the API actions.

quotes: The name is displayed in the audit logs as the entity performing the API actions.

notification-module.title: Which module covers IaC scan failures, and who receives notification emails
notification-module.detail: The Module field lists only Data Collection or Vulnerability Management, yet IaC scan failures are listed as notifications; which module covers them is not stated, and neither is who receives the notification emails.

audit-log-scope.title: What audit log retention and CSV export cover beyond the stated limits
audit-log-scope.detail: The page gives 60 days of viewable history but not whether older events are kept, and does not say whether the CSV export honours filters. The event list is a flat set of bullets mixing module headings and actions, so which action belongs to which module is partly inferred.

guide-step-5.title: What Step 5 of the step-by-step guide is
guide-step-5.detail: The guide lists Steps 1 to 4 and then 6 to 11; Step 5 is missing from the captured page.
